# cfDNA fetal fraction and CPI estimation

The bundled NIPAT implementation integrates NEWPAT commit
`9c2a8be60afcb944153710da6a61cd0559e2b4cf`, retaining NIPAT's cached input reading,
ordered parallel threshold evaluation and paginated plots. Run it through the
NIPAT runtime, which supplies the configuration and execution helpers.

All genotype thresholds, the Other-read threshold, minimum fetal-read support,
SNP/DNP mismatch constants and logCPI plot guides can be inspected with
`nipat settings cpi` and changed using `--set cpi.PARAMETER=VALUE` or a
`--scientific-config` JSON file. Every run records its effective settings and
readable model constants. `--cutoff_map` retains multiple named panels; their
complete curves are written under `curves/`. Summaries also record
`Min_fetal_reads` and `Marker_type`.

In native R invocations, explicit arguments override configuration values.
`--err_const` overrides the constant of the detected marker type, including an
explicit `--err_const_snp` or `--err_const_dnp`; the other type is unchanged.
`scientific-settings.json` in the output directory records the final parameters
after these overrides, together with the model constants.

This module estimates fetal fraction and calculates the Combined Paternity Index (CPI) from maternal cfDNA and putative-father count tables generated by [SNPcall](../SNPcall) or [DNPcall](https://github.com/fravasini/DNPcall).

A single script supports both marker types and produces CPI curves across increasing minimum minor-allele read thresholds, together with pair-specific plots and a summary table.

For details on the calling workflow, see the [DNPcall documentation](https://github.com/fravasini/DNPcall).

## Requirements

- R ≥ 4.2.0
- R packages: `dplyr`, `readxl`, `ggplot2`, `patchwork`, `argparse`, `stringr`, and `tidyr`

## Installation

```bash
git clone https://github.com/lpistacchia/NEWPAT.git
cd NEWPAT/CPI_from_cffDNA
```

## Inputs

Required inputs are:

- Maternal cfDNA and putative-father calling output tables.
- A population-frequency table for the markers contributing to the CPI.

An optional SNP or DNP list can restrict the analysis to a specific panel.

### Calling outputs

Place the SNPcall or DNPcall `.txt` output tables in one directory. Files must include coordinates, `REF`, `ALT`, `N_REF`, `N_ALT`, `N_Other`, and `total_count`.

### Population frequencies

Provide a tab-separated file with a header:

| Type | Required columns |
|---|---|
| SNP | `chr`, `pos`, `Ref_f.pop`, `Alt_f.pop` |
| DNP | `chr`, `pos1`, `pos2`, `Ref_f.pop`, `Alt_f.pop` |

`Ref_f.pop` and `Alt_f.pop` must correspond to the REF and ALT alleles in the calling outputs. If the frequency table includes `REF` and `ALT`, their agreement is checked.

### Optional marker list

Use `--markers` to restrict both fetal-fraction estimation and CPI calculation to a panel. The column order is:

| Type | Columns |
|---|---|
| SNP | `chr`, `pos`, `ref`, `alt` |
| DNP | `chr`, `pos1`, `pos2`, `ref`, `alt` |

Lists with or without a header are accepted. Coordinates are 1-based.

When a list is supplied, every listed marker must have associated population frequencies. The frequency table may contain additional markers.

Without `--markers`, fetal-fraction estimation uses all eligible sites in the calling outputs. Only sites with associated population frequencies can contribute to the CPI.

## Usage

```bash
Rscript cfDNA_CPI_estimator.R \
  --pileup_dir path/to/calling_outputs \
  --out_dir results_CPI \
  --pairs "A1:A1,A2:A2" \
  --mother_prefix Mother \
  --father_prefix Father \
  --popfreq path/to/population_frequencies.txt
```

This example analyses `MotherA1.txt` with `FatherA1.txt` and `MotherA2.txt` with `FatherA2.txt`.

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `--pileup_dir` | Directory containing the calling output tables |
| `--out_dir` | Output directory |
| `--pairs` | Maternal:paternal identifiers, separated by commas |
| `--mother_prefix` | Filename prefix preceding the maternal identifier |
| `--father_prefix` | Filename prefix preceding the paternal identifier |
| `--popfreq` | Population-frequency table |
| `--markers` | Optional SNP or DNP marker list |
| `--min_fetal_reads` | Minimum minor-allele read support; default: `2` |
| `--err_const_snp` | SNP mismatch constant; default: `0.001` |
| `--err_const_dnp` | DNP mismatch constant; default: `0.0000892303778101497` |

The marker type is detected automatically, and the script checks coordinate and allele consistency.

### Minimum read support

`--min_fetal_reads` sets the minimum number of reads supporting the minor allele at a maternal-informative site.

The default is `2`. To require at least five reads, add:

```bash
--min_fetal_reads 5
```

This parameter controls informative-site selection, the sites used for fetal-fraction estimation, and the starting threshold of the CPI curve. It must be a positive integer.

### Mismatch constants

At informative sites where the putative father is homozygous for the maternal allele, the PI uses a mismatch constant in place of zero.

The script selects the SNP or DNP constant automatically. To change it, add the corresponding option, for example:

```bash
--err_const_snp 0.0012
```

Values are proportions, not percentages. The defaults are specific to this workflow and can be adjusted for other datasets. The value used is recorded in the log and summary table.

## Outputs

### Summary table

`Summary_FetalFraction_CPI.csv` contains one row per maternal–paternal pair.

| Column | Description |
|---|---|
| `Pair` | Pair identifier and marker type |
| `N_sites_mother` | Maternal-informative sites retained |
| `N_sites_father` | Retained sites also present in the filtered paternal table |
| `Median_fetal_fraction_raw` | Median site-level fetal-fraction estimate |
| `Median_fetal_fraction_percent` | Median fetal-fraction estimate as a percentage |
| `Max_logCPI`, `Min_logCPI` | Maximum and minimum log₁₀(CPI) across read thresholds |
| `Median_logCPI`, `Mean_logCPI` | Median and mean log₁₀(CPI) across read thresholds |
| `CPI_medianFF` | log₁₀(CPI) at the threshold nearest the rounded median minor-allele read count |
| `Error_constant` | Mismatch constant used |

### Plots

The `plots/` directory contains one PDF per pair and `All_CPIplots.pdf`, combining all pairs.

Plots show log₁₀(CPI) and matching and mismatching site counts across increasing minimum minor-allele read thresholds.
